course.title: Atomic – Cambridge Lower Secondary Mathematics — Stage 7

unit.title: Shapes and Symmetry
unit.blurb: Line and rotational symmetry, parts of a circle, regular and irregular polygons, congruent shapes, and 3D shapes with their nets.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Identify lines of symmetry and the order of rotational symmetry of 2D shapes.

O2.t: Know the parts of a circle and classify polygons, including regular polygons.

O3.t: Recognise congruent shapes and identify corresponding sides and angles.

O4.t: Identify and describe 3D shapes, their faces, edges and vertices, and match them to nets.

p: A **line of symmetry** splits a shape into two halves that are mirror images. If you fold along it, the halves match exactly.
A rectangle has 2 lines of symmetry; a square has 4.
A shape has **rotational symmetry** if it looks the same after a turn of less than 360°. The **order** is how many times it fits onto itself in one full turn.
The diagonals of a rectangle are NOT lines of symmetry.

p: The **centre** is the middle. The **radius** goes from the centre to the edge. The **diameter** goes across through the centre: **diameter = 2 × radius**. The **circumference** is the distance all the way round.
A **polygon** is a flat shape with straight sides. A **regular polygon** has all sides equal and all angles equal.
The radius is HALF the diameter.

**Corresponding** sides and angles are equal: if triangle ABC is congruent to PQR, then AB = PQ and angle A = angle P.
Two squares of different sizes are similar, not congruent.

A cube has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. A **net** is a flat shape that folds up to make the solid.
